FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards after the draft finalized by Textile Speciality 
Chemicals and Dyestuffs Sectional Committee had been approved by the Textile Division Council. 


The revival of natural dyes has been for two reasons: 
a) Due to the harmful effect of synthetic dyes, globally safer natural dyes are being preferred, and 


b) Ban of azo dyes has also brought back natural dyes in limelight. Natural dyes are being used extensively 
for dyeing of cotton, silk and wool substrates. 


Thus, Lac dye (Kerria lacca) has its own characteristics of being a natural dyestuff and its method of use in 
dyeing and printing these textile substrates. In order to achieve optimum quality with minimum lot to lot variation 
and variations in dyeing due to same dye of different manufacturers, it is essential to standardize this natural 
dyestuff. This will also lead to minimize cost benefit ratio and help the user to adjust his dyeing or printing recipes 
suitably. 


Lac is the scarlet resinous secretion of a number of species of lac insects, of which the most commonly cultivated 
species is Kerria lacca tree that grows between 5 and 8 m tall. Lac dye is a deep red colourant extracted from 
the crude shellac resin excreted by the lac insect, indigenous to southeast Asia. It is the coloring principle used to 
make lac lake or Indian Lake, a historical pigment used in manuscript and easel painting until the 19th century. 


Lac dyes (laccaic acid) consisting of polyphenolic anthraquinone compounds are a natural, weakly acidic, and 
reddish colourant produced by the insect Coccus lacca or Laccifer lacca and can be obtained in large amounts as 
a by product of shellac industry. 


It is for the first time that the standard for natural dyestuff Lac dye (Kerria lacca) has been forfulated, it is mainly 
for the ease of buyers, seller and users of this natural dyestuff. Standardization and identification method will 
bring all the major parameters under scan and match. The main intention of this specification is to identify the 
natural dyestuff from the synthetic analogue which is usually used as adulterant for cost modification and color 
enhancement purposes. 


The composition of the Committee responsible for the formulation of this standard is given in Annex F. 


In reporting the results of a test or analysis made in accordance with this standard, if the final value, observed or 
calculated, is to be rounded off, it shall be done in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 ‘Rules for rounding off numerical 
values (revised). 


IS 17212 : 2019 


Indian Standard 


TEXTILE DYESTUFFS — LAC DYE — 
IDENTIFICATION 


1 SCOPE 


This standard prescribes test method and identification 
requirement of dried/ aqueous extract of lac dye and 
lac dyed textiles. The detection and identification 
of synthetic lac dye and natural colorant lac dye 
are conducted using kit method given in Annex A. 
Confirmatory tests can be carried out through thin 
layer chromatography (TLC) and high performance 
liquid chromatography (HPLC) by chromatographic 
techniques as given in Annex B and C as well as 
by UV-visible spectroscopic technique as given in 
Annex D. The method for extraction of natural lac dye 
from dyed swatches is given in Annex E. 


2 REFERENCE 


The following standards contain provisions which, 
through reference in this text, constitute provisions of 
this standard. At the time of publication, the editions 
indicated were valid. All standards are subject to 
revision, and parties to agreements based on this 
standard are encouraged to investigate the possibility 
of applying the most recent editions of the standards 
indicated below.

3 TERMS AND DEFINITIONS 


For the purposes of this standard, the following terms 
and definitions apply: 


3.1 Lac Dye — The water-soluble dyestuff, lac dye, 
is composed of laccaic acid, mainly in the form of 
ammonium salts. These pigments are present at up 
to 10 percent in stick lac is harvested before adult 
insects depart from their cocoon. Processed seed lac 
and shell lac have a low content of laccaic acids but 
retain a yellow water-insoluble pigment, erythrolaccin. 
Lac consist of laccaic acid A, B, C, D and E. The main 
chemical structures of the natural lac dye is given 
in Fig. 1. 


3.2 Natural Colour — Colorants from natural origin, 
particularly materials obtained from plant parts namely, 
stem, root and leaves, extracted without any chemical 
reaction primarily used in textiles for dyeing or 
printing.

Fic. 1 CHEMICAL STRUCTURES OF THE NATURAL LAC DYE 


4 PRINCIPLE 


Natural colorants are usually never a single compound. 
They are composed of several compounds which 
are structurally similar, each of them having their 
characteristic bonding with the fabric based on 
their structure uniqueness. Their contribution in the 
total colourant may vary. Therefore, the analysis of 
these individual components can be carried out by 
chromatographic and spectroscopic techniques. The 
authenticity of the natural colourant can be established 
by these techniques very clearly. 


5PROCEDURE 


5.1 Preparation of Natural Lac and Synthetic Red 
Dye Samples 


Stock solution of natural lac sample is prepared in 
methanol containing 1000 mg/l of natural lac. This 
solution is further used after dilution, 1f necessary, for 
chromatographic and spectroscopic analyses. 


IS 17212 : 2019 


5.2 Analysis 


The detection and identification of natural lac and 
synthetic red dye samples are conducted using 
kit method given in Annex A, TLC and HPLC by 
chromatographic techniques as given in Annex B and 
Annex C as well as by UV-visible spectroscopy as 
given in Annex D. The method for extraction of natural 
dye from dyed swatches is given in Annex E. 


5.3 Qualification and Identification of Natural 
Lac Dye 


Comparison between analyses of natural lac and 
synthetic red dye through 5.3 could show the results of 
discrete differences in synthetic and natural lac sample 
in the Kit method. The specific tests to be conducted are 
given in Table 1. 


6 REPORT 
The report shall include the following information: 


a) Name of the natural dye tested; 


b) Test method used; and 
c) Identification of the natural source. 


7 CHECK OF THE ANALYTICAL SYSTEM 


A check of the procedure of analysis and instrument/ 
equipment is also essential HPLC, UV-visible 
spectrophotometer must be checked before the analysis 
of the sample. 


8 VALIDATION OF THE METHOD 


Validation of the method and calibration is carried out 
using authentic and standard natural dye for UV-visible 
spectrophotometric analysis for the following: 


a) Reliability of the method, 
b) Repeatability, and 
c) Comparability.

ANNEX A 
( Clauses 1, 5.2 and 5.3) 


KIT TEST FOR IDENTIFICATION OF NATURAL LAC DYE 


A-1 PRINCIPLE 


Each natural dye has its characteristic molecular 
composition which is the distinctive feature of that 
dyestuff. Dissolution of the two samples of lac and 
synthetic red dye under the class of red dyes in different 
polarity solvents would bring out the difference and 
distinction when compared with synthetic red dye. 
The lac dye bearing different contaminants dissolves 
in water layer better, whereas the synthetic red dye 
dissolves well in dichloromethane solvent. 


A-2 APPARATUS 

A-2.1 Test Tubes 

A-2.2 Test Tube Holder 
A-2.3 Electronic Balance 
A-2.4 Spatula 

A-2.5 pH Meter 

A-2.6 Pipette 


A-2.7 Measuring Cylinder 


A-3 REAGENTS 
A-3.1 Water 

A-3.2 Ferric Chloride 
A-3.3 Natural Lac Dye 


A-3.4 Synthetic Red Dye 
All reagents should be of analytical grade (AR). 


A-4 PROCEDURE 


Two red dyes (5-10 mg each) were dissolved in 10 ml 
of 10 percent HCl. The solution turned reddish. To this 
solution | ml of 5 percent solution of sodium hydroxide 
was added. The colour changed to blue. Appearance of 
blue colour in lac at alkaline medium is because the 
lac dye is pH sensitive. The synthetic red dye remains 
unchanged in colour. Identification of the dye by this 
method involves a specific test for natural lac and red 
dye does not respond to this test. 


A-5 OBSERVATION

Cor) mp 


Fic. 2 CHANGE IN COLOUR IN Lac DYE 


A-6 CONCLUSION 


The clear difference in colour identifies the natural lac 
dye and synthetic red dye very distinctively as shown 
in Fig. 2.

ANNEX B 
( Clauses 1, 5.2 and 5.3 ) 


CHROMATOGRAPHIC ANALYSIS -- THIN LAYER CHROMATOGRAPHY 


B-1 PRINCIPLE 


TLC is also used to support the identity of a compound 
in a mixture when the R, of a compound is compared 
with the R, of a known compound (preferably both run 
on the same TLC plate). Natural lac dyes and synthetic 
red dyes are compared on TLC. 


B-2 APPARATUS 


B-2.1 Silica Coated TLC plates 

B-2.2 TLC Capillary 

B-2.3 TLC Elution Chamber 

B-2.4 TLC Iodine Chamber 

B-2.5 Electronic Balance — Resolution at 0.001 g. 
B-2.6 Spatula 

B-2.7 Sonicator — To be set at (45 + 2) °C. 


B-2.8 Measuring Cylinder 


B-3 REAGENTS 


B-3.1 Natural Lac Dye 
B-3.2 Synthetic Red Dye 
B-3.3 Ethyl Acetate 
B-3.4 Hexane 

B-3.5 Dichloromethane 


B-3.6 Silica Gel (TLC Grade) 
All reagents should be of analytical grade (AR). 


B-4 PROCEDURE 


TLC studies were carried out with dye extract in 
EtOAc using 50 percent EtOAc: Hexane as suitable 
eluent system for red dyes. The spots are visualized in 
visible light as well as in iodine chamber. The possible 
constituents of the extracts are identified by comparing 
TLC data, that is, color of the spot and R, values of 
natural lac and synthetic red dye.

ANNEX C 
( Clauses 1, 5.2 and 5.3) 


IDENTIFICATION OF NATURAL LAC DYE BY HIGH PERFORMANCE 
LIQUID CHROMATOGRAPHY (HPLC) METHOD 


C-1 PRINCIPLE 


Identification of compounds by HPLC is a crucial part 
of any HPLC assay. In order to identify any compound 
by HPLC, a detector must first be selected. UV detector 
may be selected and set to optimal detection setting 
and develop a separation assay. The parameters of this 
assay shall be made to be such that a clean peak of the 
both the samples are observed from the chromatograph. 


C-2 APPARATUS 


C-2.1 HPLC Machine 

C-2.2 PDA Detector 

C-2.3 C-18 Reverse Phase Column (RPC-C18) 
C-2.4 Electronic Balance — Resolution at 0.001g. 
C-2.5 Binary Pump System 

C-2.6 Measuring Cylinder 

C-2.7 Spatula 

C-2.8 Micro Syringe 

C-3 REAGENTS 


C-3.1 Methanol 
C-3.2 De-ionized Water 


C-3.3 Natural Lac Dye 
NOTE — All solvents used should be HPLC grade only. 


C-4 PROCEDURE 


Identification of compounds by HPLC is a crucial part 
of any HPLC assay. In order to identify any compound 
by HPLC, a detector must first be selected. UV detector 


PSV LAC A001:1 UV2 300nm 


may be selected and set to optimal detection settings, a 
separation assay to developed. The parameters of this 
assay may be made such that a clean peak of the both 
the samples are observed from the chromatograph. The 
experimental conditions are as following: 


a) Column: C18 Flow rate: 0.8 ml/min; 
b) Detection wavelengths: 300 nm; 


c) Flow scheme: (eluent A= 0.2 percent TFA in water 
and eluent B = 0.2 percent TFA in Acetonitrile); 
and 


d) Linear gradient: 0-100 percent B 


Due care is to be taken in identifying peak so that 
a reasonable retention time well separated from 
extraneous peaks at the detection levels. Clear 
observation can be made from the lac dye sample as 
can be seen in the chromatographs given in Fig. 4.

ANNEX D 
( Clauses 1, 5.2 and 5.3 ) 


IDENTIFICATION OF NATURAL LAC DYE BY UV-VISIBLE 
SPECTROSCOPIC METHOD 


D-1 PRINCIPLE 


When sample molecules are exposed to light having 
an energy that matches a possible electronic transition 
within the molecule, some of the light energy will be 
absorbed as the electron is promoted to a higher energy 
orbital. An optical spectrometer records the wavelengths 
at which absorption occurs together with the degree of 
absorption at each wavelength. The resulting spectrum 
is presented as a graph of absorbance (A) versus 
wavelength. 


Many molecules absorb ultraviolet or visible light. The 
absorbance of a solution increases as attenuation of the 
beam increases. Absorbance is directly proportional 
to the path length, b, and the concentration, c, of the 
absorbing species. Beer 5 law states that: 


A= Ebc 


Where, € is a constant of proportionality, called the 
absorbtivity. 


Different molecules absorb radiation of different 
wavelengths. An absorption spectrum will show a 
number of absorption bands corresponding to structural 
groups within the molecule. Thus, the absorption 
spectra (optical density) of a particular dye at a 
particular wavelength is maximum. 


D-2 APPARATUS 


D-2.1 Ultra Violet — Visible spectrophotometer 
machine. 


Scan Graph 


3.5 4.0, 3.295

D-2.2 Quartz Sample Tube (Cuvette)

D-2.3 Electronic Balance — Resolution at 0.001g 
D-2.4 Spatula 
D-2.5 Whatmann Filter Paper — Grade 42 


D-3 REAGENT 


D-3.1 Natural Lac Dye 
D-3.2 Methanol 


D-3.3 Dichloromethane 
NOTE — All reagents shall be of analytical purity. 


D-4 PROCEDURE 


Weigh 0.1 g of the natural lac dye and dissolve in 
1000 ml dichloromethane and scanned through 
UV-visible spectrometer. For visible spectrum the 
prepared solution is used and for UV spectrum the 
solution is further diluted by 5 times. Identification 
of the dye by this method involves an empirical 
comparison of the details of the spectrum that is, 
lamda maxima (optical density) of natural lac and 
the characteristic peaks are matched as shown in 
Fig. 5. The ultraviolet (UV) region scanned is normally 
from 200 to 400 nm and the visible portion is from 400 
to 800 nm.

ANNEX E 
( Clause 1, 5.2 and 5.3 ) 


EXTRACTION OF NATURAL LAC DYE FROM DYED SWATCHES 


E-1 PRINCIPLE 


The solvent (in soxhlet) extraction of dyed samples 
is necessary to release the dyes from the dyed fabric 
samples. 


E-2 PROCEDURE 


The solvent (in soxhlet) extraction of dyed samples 
is necessary to release the dyes from the dyed cotton 
samples. 50 gm of cotton samples, dyed from natural 


lac dye is cut into small pieces and packed in a filter 
paper as a filter paper column. The packed filter paper 
column is put for soxhlet extraction for 6-8 h with 
methanol as solvent for extraction, temperature is set 
at 60°C. Till all the colour is discharged. Remove the 
solvent in a vacuum rotatory evaporator to dryness. The 
sample is now ready for used in chromatographic and 
spectroscopic analysis as per the methods described 
above.
